This opt-in pilot adds PKPT03, PKPL01 and linear PKCG03 entries alongside the existing TLG catalog. It does not replace the catalog or change NCA estimators. Outputs are exploratory prototypes, not validated submission templates.

## Use the pilot

Install `cards >= 0.9.0`, `gtsummary >= 2.6.1`, `gt >= 1.4.0` and `crane >= 0.3.2`. They are optional dependencies; existing outputs do not require them. Word export also uses the existing `officer` and `flextable` dependencies. The package requires R >= 4.4; this pilot was exercised on R 4.4.3 and R 4.5.2. The four new dependencies declare R minima no higher than 4.2. Current crane also requires dplyr >= 1.2.0 and ggplot2 >= 4.0.0, so installing it can upgrade those packages. The pilot leaves the existing CI matrix and check policy unchanged. R 4.4 compatibility was tested separately; see the dependency audit below for its unresolved check NOTE.

The R 4.4 macOS binary repository had older versions of the four pilot packages during validation. Installing their current sources into an isolated R 4.4 library passed the pilot tests; other dependencies came from public R 4.4 binaries. If available binaries are below the required minima, use:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("cards", "gt", "gtsummary", "crane"), type = "source")
```

After running NCA, open **TLG**, choose **Add TLG**, search for **NEST**, add all three pilots and submit the order. The existing defaults remain selected unless removed. Use the table/listing/graph sidebar to select parameters, grouping, statistics, axes and annotations. `$VAR` inserts values and `!VAR` inserts labels. Table and listing defaults split by analyte, specimen and dose occasion; missing split columns are ignored. Add visit or interval variables if a reporting cell still contains different measurements. Conflicting duplicates produce an explanation instead of silently choosing the first value.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
summary <- t_pkpt03_nest(adpp, stats = c("n", "Mean", "SD"),
                         param_filter = c("Max Conc", "AUC to Last Nonzero Conc"),
                         title = "PK summary: $PPCAT")
listing <- l_pkpl01_nest(adpp, param_filter = "Max Conc")
graphs <- g_pkcg03_lin_nest(adnca, plotly = FALSE)
attr(summary[[1]], "tlg_data") # Numeric results before presentation
attr(summary[[1]], "tlg_ard")  # Presentation analysis results data
```

Export via **Export as ZIP**, selecting the rendered TLG outputs and their formats. CSV and XLSX preserve numeric values and complete listing keys. PDF, HTML and DOCX retain titles, subtitles, units and footnotes; CSV/XLSX annotations are in an accompanying `annotations.csv` file, referenced in the manifest. HTML and DOCX table/listing export is limited to the pilots; requests for those formats on legacy tables are recorded as skipped. Existing graph PNG/PDF/HTML paths continue to work. Wide tables should be narrowed using parameter/statistic selection; Word pagination and repeated keys across page boundaries need inspection before use in a report. No RTF or ASCII `.out` export is added.

Rendered tables and listings use compact default headers and left-aligned row keys. Custom labels take precedence. The summary suppresses repeated parent strata before the parameter column, while keeping each parameter and unit visible; the listing suppresses repeated keys within parent groups. CSV/XLSX retain complete keys and the existing metadata labels. Default splits and grouping remain configurable: add `AVISIT` to summary splits or listing keys when reporting separate visits. This presentation update does not introduce a new population filter or treatment-level N.

A full mixed pilot/legacy order exported in every format took about 14 minutes locally, producing a 26.8 MB ZIP. Narrow the order and format selection for quicker iteration; this pilot does not optimize legacy graph capture.

## Calculation and ARD choices

PKPT03 calls `t_pkpt03_col()` and its shared ADPP summary helper. It keeps n, arithmetic mean, sample SD, CV, geometric mean, geometric CV, median, minimum and maximum, with existing rounding. Presentation preserves these decimals regardless of value magnitude or the session's `digits` option. `PPSUMXF == "Y"` records are omitted. n counts values that are not missing; geometric statistics use positive values only. Equal repeated subject/visit records retain the legacy first-row convention. The pilot rejects conflicting duplicates, including a missing first value followed by one with a value. Units are explicit row strata, preventing incompatible values from being pooled. A missing result with a missing unit may therefore appear as a separate n=0 row. Partial AUC windows share one `PARAM`; the pilot appends each supplied `PPSTINT`/`PPENINT` interval (for example `AUC from T1 to T2 (PT0H-PT2H)`) so each window is summarized and listed separately, even when subjects have complementary windows or summary exclusions leave only one window per subject. Summary exclusions are applied before interval naming, so excluded windows cannot change the grouping of eligible urine results. This grouping differs from the legacy table, which keeps the first interval per subject. Known urine parameters with one collection interval per subject keep their name and pool as in the legacy table, even when actual collection end times differ. The existing parameter metadata identifies urine parameters using the first value per row that is not missing or blank, from `PARAMCD`, `PPTESTCD` and the parameter name; missing, empty and whitespace-only codes fall through to the next source. Custom urine labels therefore need a recognized parameter code to retain pooling. Unknown parameters with interval bounds remain separated rather than silently pooling different windows. The default subtitle is the split key, used verbatim rather than parsed as annotation syntax; a custom subtitle is followed by the split key, so every preview and export identifies its split.

The resulting numeric cells become a `cards` object consumed by `gtsummary::tbl_ard_wide_summary()`. This preserves calculations already reviewed in aNCA instead of recomputing through `tbl_summary()` or `cardx`. The ARD `variable` and `stat_name` fields are local row/statistic identifiers, with original grouping columns retained and `tlg_ard_columns` mapping statistic identifiers back to result columns. It is an intermediate presentation ARD, not a CDISC Analysis Results Standard dataset; it holds the already-rounded results and does not pass `cards::check_ard_structure()`, which expects a `method` row. A broader migration would need stable analysis identifiers, standardized result metadata and provenance rather than exporting this intermediate object as a submission artifact.

PKPL01 shares the legacy listing preparation, filters and three-decimal numeric rounding, then uses `crane::tbl_listing()`. The summary and listing share hierarchical repeated-key suppression instead of crane's independent suppression of each key. Displayed values use the same fixed-decimal formatting as the summary, so previews, HTML and Word show the rounded values regardless of the session's `digits` option. Child keys stay visible when their parent changes, so a repeated subject identifier in a new treatment remains visible. Values are never blanked in the data export. Individual listings retain summary-excluded records, as existing listings do; they are not summary populations. Known units must agree per parameter and split. A value that is not missing without a unit is rejected when the selected unit column exists; missing results without units remain permitted. Empty and whitespace-only unit fields count as missing; a known unit on another row supplies the header for both the pilot and legacy listings. Omitting the unit column omits unit labels. When missing split keys remove every record, the listing displays a no-data explanation.

PKCG03 delegates to `g_pkcg03_lin()` and retains Plotly interactivity plus the source ggplot for static export. Mean plus/minus SD remains the default. The wrapper resolves annotations separately for each split and appends an explicit methods footnote. `PKSUMXF` exclusions, more than one distinct subject and no more than 50% BLQ at a timepoint/group remain the existing reporting rules. The BLQ rule needs an `AVALC` or `AVALCAT1` flag; without one (as in the example data) nothing is removed for BLQ, and the footnote says so instead of claiming the rule. Numeric `AVAL` values are used as supplied, including upstream imputation; the pilot does no new BLQ imputation. Empty or all-missing results produce explanations.

NCA estimators and summary formulas remain unchanged; interval grouping is the explicit reporting change described above. Separate decisions are needed before changing other existing behavior: graph SE/CI currently use the record count including missing values as the denominator, repeated records can therefore affect means/intervals, and BLQ detection recognizes the existing character patterns rather than every possible threshold string (for example `<0.1`). Changing those rules, automatically preferring a later duplicate with a value, or adopting the current preview catalog's `ANL02FL` population filter would require dedicated specifications and validation. These rules are deliberately documented rather than silently changed here.

## Deviations from the NEST references

The preview catalog was rechecked on 2026-11-10 against examples rendered with `tlg.templates` 0.1.0.9004. It includes PKPT03, PKPL01 and PKCG03. These examples are versioned references, not evidence that the pilot conforms to every catalog requirement. Matching the original aNCA results and reproducing the official template are separate checks.

The current PKPT03 example separates `AVISIT` onto pages, includes treatment-level N from `ANL02FL == "Y"` concentration data, combines parameter names with units, and uses `crane::pk_param_sort()` for parameter labels and order. It computes statistics with `gtsummary::tbl_wide_summary()` and extracts their ARD with `gather_ard()`. Most statistics use `crane::fmt_3sig()`, while CV values use `fmt_pct()`. The pilot retains aNCA's existing rounded statistics, separate unit keys and presentation ARD. It does not infer an eligible-population N from the ADPP records supplied to the summary API. The per-parameter n already shown is not interchangeable with that treatment-level N.

The current PKPL01 example uses three significant figures, orders and labels parameters with `pk_param_sort()`, and includes treatment, a site/patient identifier derived from `SITEID`/`SUBJID`, and `AVISIT`. The pilot retains aNCA's three-decimal rounding and `USUBJID`, supports configurable listing keys, and suppresses repeated keys within their parent groups. Its natural dose ordering can differ from the legacy text listing; missing numeric results appear as blanks rather than `NA`. Neither change removes records or changes the numeric export.

The current PKCG03 code uses `crane::gg_pkc_lineplot()`, filters `ANL02FL == "Y"`, and plots `NFRLT`, explicitly labeled as nominal time from first dose. Its programming notes still specify nominal time from last dose. This is an inconsistency within the reference: the pilot retains aNCA's first-dose default and existing estimators, exclusions and BLQ rules; `NRRLT` remains selectable under X axis. Adopting the crane graph or its population filter needs a separate same-data comparison and an agreed population definition.

The workshop and current examples decorate with `citril::decorate_tlg()` and use ARDs for QC. The pilot decorates through `gt` and `officer`; HTML and Word use formatted tables, while PDF retains the existing text-table export. The pilot supports crane 0.3.2, which does not export the current examples' `pk_param_sort()` or `fmt_3sig()` helpers. Using a newer catalog example does not establish that those helpers are available at the pilot's minimum dependency versions.

The programming notes refer to Overall Requirements and Appendix 2 for population and precision rules, but those specifications were not linked from the inspected pages or supplied separately. The example code and workshop do not fill that specification gap. The pilot preserves aNCA behavior where a change would require a scientific or population decision.

## Integration and migration boundary

The catalog entries inherit existing sidebar options in `inst/shiny/tlg.yaml`. `tlg_module.R` renders `gtsummary` through the shared gt adapter and preserves the text rendering of legacy listings. `tab_tlg.R` keeps the existing submitted-order registry, with dependency checks performed per output so crane listings can work without `rlistings`. `tlg_export.R` consumes the same resolved objects and adds rendered documents and annotation sidecars. `tab_nca/zip.R` exposes the extra format choices.

The settings/labels work around #1476/#1528 and #1450 may touch the same catalog, module option defaults, annotation parsing, column labels and export helpers. This branch uses only main's interfaces. Current settings export does not persist TLG orders or per-output sidebar edits; this pilot does not add that persistence. A future integration should preserve the numeric `tlg_data` contract, resolved `tlg_annotations`, complete flat-file keys and the graph's stored ggplot, then test label and settings restoration together. The shared listing preparation is the other likely merge point.

The NEST workshop's package map supports `gtsummary`/`crane`, `cards`/`cardx` and ggplot2, with `citril` for decoration/export. This bounded pilot uses aNCA's existing registry/export architecture and public packages; it does not add `citril`, internal `NEST.TLGs`/`tlg.templates`, a catalog-wide migration or a new study-data model. Evaluate standardized pagination and metadata before extending the pilot.

## Reproduce the validation

### Dependency audit

The R 4.4 job used during validation at commit `c7787d686` failed because `--as-cran` reported a NOTE for more than 20 non-default Imports: aNCA had 25, with zero check errors or warnings. The pilot adds four Suggests and no Imports. The redundant direct `magrittr` dependency was removed because its only use, `%>%`, is already re-exported by `dplyr`. This leaves 24 non-default Imports and does not resolve the dependency NOTE.

The remaining dependencies have runtime uses: `PKNCA` and `units` provide calculations and conversions; `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `purrr`, `rlang` and `glue` prepare data and annotations; `ggplot2`, `plotly`, `formatters`, `htmltools` and `htmlwidgets` render or label outputs; `writexl`, `yaml` and `zip` write workbooks, settings and archives. The app uses `shiny`, `bslib`, `logger`, `reactable`, `reactable.extras`, `shinycssloaders`, `shinyjs`, `shinyjqui` and `shinyWidgets` for its interface, logging, editable tables, loading indicators and slope selection. None can simply be moved to Suggests without changing the supported runtime or adding conditional behavior. The pilot does not change CI to accept this NOTE or add a dedicated R 4.4 job. The existing workflow retains its configured failure policy, which defaults to failing on notes. The R 4.4 dependency NOTE remains unresolved; passing pilot tests establishes functional compatibility, not a clean `R CMD check` on that version. Any broader dependency reduction or CI policy change requires separate review.

### Numerical and export checks

From a checkout with development dependencies installed, run:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/validate_nest_pilot.R /tmp/nest-evidence
```

`data-raw/rebuild.R` skips this script. It reruns NCA on the checked-in `data-raw/adnca_example.csv`, compares pilot summaries/listings/graphs to legacy outputs with equivalent grouping, independently calculates mean/SD/n from source rows, and writes numeric evidence plus a ZIP containing a compact report. The unit tests additionally exercise all nine summary statistics, exclusions, BLQ-heavy timepoints, empty/all-missing/single-subject data, units, grouping comparisons, conflicting/equal duplicates and repeated-key suppression. Integration tests inspect sidebar output, CSV/XLSX values, Word content, HTML annotations and ZIP contents.

### Installed-app settings and generated-script replay

On 2026-10-30, a fresh installed app was exercised through upload, mapping, filtering, NCA, TLG selection and ZIP download in Chrome on R 4.5.2. This exposed missing namespace qualification in versioned settings restoration and export validation, plus an incorrect input-data path in the downloaded script. Those defects are corrected and covered by regression tests that do not expose private package objects on the app's search path.

To repeat the workflow:

1. Upload `data-raw/adnca_example.csv`, accept the standard mapping and filtering, and run NCA for the default serum/first-dose selection. Change the integration method to `linear` and minimum half-life points to 4, then rerun NCA.
2. Add the three NEST pilots alongside the existing outputs. Select Max Conc and AUC to Last Nonzero Conc for the summary and listing, and n/Mean/SD for the summary. Use `PARAM` and `TRT01A` as summary strata and `USUBJID` and `TRT01A` as listing keys. Set titles to `Replay summary: $PPCAT` and `Replay listing: $PPCAT`, and add `Replay verification` as the summary and graph footnote.
3. Download the versioned settings. Start a fresh app session, upload the same source data and saved settings, and let the restored NCA run finish. Compare the settings, mapping, filters, slope selections and all CDISC datasets with the original session. Select the same TLG order and sidebar values again, since those are not persisted by the settings format.
4. Export PP, ADPP, ADNCA, pre-specifications, settings and the R script through the ZIP dialog. Extract the ZIP, set the working directory to its root and run the unedited `session_code.R` in a fresh R session. Compare its `cdisc_data` with the app results, then call the three pilot functions with the same options to compare their numeric data and annotations.

The settings replay matched PP and ADPP (192 rows each) and ADNCA (1,308 rows), including attributes. Settings, mapping, filters and slope selections also matched. The stored unit overrides are sparse after restoration; the effective units and dataset values matched. Both analyte splits of the pilot summary and listing, all five graph datasets and their annotations, and both splits of the retained legacy summary matched after applying the same TLG options. The unedited generated script reproduced the same three CDISC datasets and pilot results. Independent source values 3.597, 4.556 and 3.660 reproduced Cmax n=3, mean=3.938 and sample SD=0.536.

The separate validation script also passed during that validation: 1,308 source records, 1,704 ADPP records across its broader selections, 112 independent summary rows and 448 graph cells. Pilot CSV/XLSX/PDF/HTML/DOCX and graph PNG/PDF/HTML exports succeeded; unsupported legacy table HTML/DOCX requests were recorded as skipped. That full test suite passed 3,837 assertions with one inherited plotting warning and three existing skips (unavailable `arrow`, the disabled E2E runner and the full-session slide-export case). The real-app replay above was run separately from that disabled runner. Local `R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual` completed with zero errors, warnings or notes on R 4.5.2, which reports the excessive Imports count as informational; this does not establish an R 4.4 pass.

The presentation update was checked on 2026-11-10 with R 4.5.2. With aligned settings, all nine statistics across 24 summary splits (832 rows), 168 listing records (1,704 parameter cells), and 448 graph cells matched an isolated copy of unmodified main at `1da57b789`; all plotted layers also matched. This used the real NCA data saved by the validation above. Fresh CSV/XLSX/PDF/HTML/DOCX exports retained numeric results, complete flat-file keys, units and annotations. HTML, Word and PDF output was visually inspected, including PDF continuation columns. The full source suite passed 3,906 assertions with the same one warning and three skips. These checks establish parity with aNCA under equivalent settings; they are not a same-data execution of the internal catalog templates. A full package check and the complete installed-app workflow were not repeated for this presentation update.

- [NEST 2.0 preview catalog](https://docs.roche.com/doc/tlg-catalog/preview/), including the code and programming notes for [PKPT03](https://docs.roche.com/doc/tlg-catalog/preview/CATALOG/GDSR_PKPT03/ARTICLE-PKPT03.html), [PKPL01](https://docs.roche.com/doc/tlg-catalog/preview/CATALOG/GDSR_PKPL01/ARTICLE-PKPL01.html) and [PKCG03](https://docs.roche.com/doc/tlg-catalog/preview/CATALOG/GDSR_PKCG03/ARTICLE-PKCG03.html), rechecked 2026-11-10 with `tlg.templates` 0.1.0.9004. The rendered PKPT03 PDF was also inspected
- [`gtsummary` wide ARD summaries](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_ard_wide_summary.html) and [ARD summaries](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_ard_summary.html)
